_comment: Capabilities this repository's documents (or its own API contracts) CLAIM,
that the code does not do as claimed. The shape is gnomon's
conformance/declared_not_implemented.json, widened from enumeration values to
capabilities, because this repository's gap is wider: the Sep 2026 audit found
docs marking a finished Phase 1 over heuristics, a constant confidence
interval and an LLM layer nothing calls.
Every entry carries:
claimed_in  where the claim is made, as {at: 'file:line', says: <quote>}.
'file@rev:line' cites a committed revision (the claim was
published there and has since been withdrawn from the tree).
reality     one line: what the code actually does.
evidence    code locations that make `reality` true, same {at, says} shape.
leaves_by   what must exist for the entry to leave the list: a test (path +
what it asserts), a CI run, or a retraction of the claim.
status      declared-not-implemented | partial | planned -- the same token
docs/CURRENT_STAGE.md shows for it.
scripts/status_claims.py checks every citation: the quote must still be in
the cited file (on the cited line, or it reports the drift). A quote that is
GONE fails the gate, because then this register says something about the code
or the docs that is no longer true -- which is the defect it exists to catch.
An entry leaves this list by being IMPLEMENTED (its leaves_by exists and
passes) or by the claim being RETRACTED from the docs -- never by being
dropped. When one leaves, it moves to `left_the_list` with the commit and the
test that pins it.

declared_not_implemented.capability: Counterfactual reasoning over a structural causal model

claimed_in.says: Structural causal model (SCM), observation, query (intervention or counterfactual)
Estimated counterfactual distribution
scm.counterfactual(observation, intervention)

declared_not_implemented.reality: No structural causal model is fitted anywhere. counterfactual_reason is now a labelled heuristic that reports identification_status NOT_ASSESSED and makes no quantitative claim (it previously reported IDENTIFIED from edge confidences and invented impact-reduction percentages). causal-core refuses rung-3 queries with RUNG_MISMATCH.

leaves_by.asserts: for a known SCM and observed unit, the counterfactual outcome under do(T=t') equals the analytic value (and equals the factual outcome when t' is the factual treatment)

declared_not_implemented.capability: Causal discovery: candidate edges and independence tests from data

claimed_in.says: Proposes candidate edges, confounders, mediators, and missing variables in the causal graph from data and document evidence.

declared_not_implemented.reality: The discovery agent proposes one edge between two freshly generated uuid4() nodes with a confidence looked up from the Cynefin domain; conditional_independence_test is a stub that returns None.

leaves_by.asserts: on data simulated from a known DAG the recovered skeleton/CPDAG is within a pre-registered structural Hamming distance of the truth

claimed_in.says: Provider-agnostic LLM
the LLM factory resolves capability → provider at runtime
Routing is handled by `src/agents/llm_factory.py`
`src/agents/llm_factory.py` emits LLMInvocation metadata (implemented)
`src/agents/llm_factory.py` capture hook | Implemented
Every LLM call via `get_llm(session_id=..., agent_id=...)` auto-captures invocation metadata

declared_not_implemented.reality: get_llm has no call site outside its own docstring: no agent invokes an LLM, and every agent's reasoning is rule or heuristic code.

leaves_by.asserts: an agent path requests a capability through get_llm and its output depends on the (stubbed) model's reply

Critical safety properties verified by this spec

declared_not_implemented.capability: Triangulation flags outcome-model misspecification in causal-core

claimed_in.says: Its power was 0.04 at n = 2,000

declared_not_implemented.reality: Measured power against a planted misspecification that biases regression adjustment by ~0.16 (~1.2 SE of the difference): 0.04 at n=2,000 (reported), 1.00 at n=50,000 (gated). At moderate n, 'estimators agree' is weak evidence that a model is right.

leaves_by.asserts: a pre-registered triangulation power >= 0.80 at n <= 5,000 against a planted misspecification, e.g. via an added specification test or flexible-learner arm

claimed_in.says: Estimation for general ID functionals

declared_not_implemented.reality: causal-core identifies such effects and returns the ID expression, then refuses with NO_ESTIMATOR: no estimator for arbitrary ID functionals exists.

leaves_by.asserts: a napkin-graph estimation case in T0 with bias <= 3 MCSE and pre-registered coverage

declared_not_implemented.capability: causal-core methods beyond the current portfolio: nonparametric front-door, discovery, time series, interference between units

claimed_in.says: Nonparametric front-door
Discovery

declared_not_implemented.reality: Listed as not implemented in the package README; none of these exists in the kernel. (Anytime-valid sequential tests left this entry on 2026-09-25 with T6; cluster-randomized designs, which handle dependence within clusters but not spillovers between them, arrived the same day with T7, and switchback designs with T8.)

leaves_by.asserts: each method leaves this entry separately, with its own pre-registered T0 case and seeded defect

declared_not_implemented.capability: Positivity violations detected before estimation

claimed_in.says: positivity and overlap

declared_not_implemented.reality: The check reads a logistic propensity model. IHDP's by-construction overlap violation (all treated children of non-white mothers removed) was not detected from its 25 covariates in 100/100 realizations; the ATE was answered by extrapolation (coverage stayed >= 0.97).

evidence.says: a refusal needs a detectable overlap violation

leaves_by.asserts: a pre-registered IHDP bar that the ATE is refused or flagged for the overlap violation, e.g. via a flexible or covariate-profile overlap check

declared_not_implemented.capability: The decision chain's head digest anchored outside the writer's control

claimed_in.says: **What the chain does not do.** It makes tampering *detectable*, not impossible

declared_not_implemented.reality: The chain is built, persisted, served and verified, and decision_records is append-only in the production schema. Both ends of anchoring now exist in code: GET /api/v1/decisions/checkpoint returns the head to publish, and POST /api/v1/decisions/verify-anchored checks the chain against checkpoints kept elsewhere, catching a rewrite that re-seals every later entry (which /verify passes) and a truncation below a checkpoint. What does not exist is the publishing: nothing sends a checkpoint to a store the platform cannot rewrite, so until a deployment does, the ledger still evidences internal consistency only.

evidence.says: A pass means the chain is *internally* consistent. It cannot mean more than
A tamper-evident record of what was decided, on what evidence, by whom.

leaves_by.asserts: the head digest is published to a store the platform cannot rewrite, and a chain rewritten in the database is detected by comparison with the published head

declared_not_implemented.capability: Finding which subgroups an effect differs across, rather than testing declared ones
declared_not_implemented.reality: No document claims it: ROADMAP.md lists subgroup discovery as missing. causal_core.segments estimates effects within subgroups the caller declares in advance and corrects for how many were examined. Nothing searches for subgroups, and this is deliberate: a subgroup chosen after looking is not covered by the correction, and honest post-hoc subgroup discovery needs machinery (sample splitting, or a method with its own guarantees) that is not here.

leaves_by.asserts: a discovered subgroup's reported interval covers its true effect at the nominal rate under a pre-registered discovery procedure, on data where no subgroup differs

declared_not_implemented.capability: Agent evaluation endpoints (consistency, calibration, decision quality) measure the running platform

claimed_in.says: summary="Agent confidence calibration probe",
summary="Composite decision quality index",
| `POST /api/v1/platform/evaluation/calibration` | Confidence calibration check |
8-run consistency probe quantifies the 37% lab-vs-production gap
Confidence calibration measured per agent, detectable within single session

declared_not_implemented.reality: None of the three observes an agent. /evaluation/consistency scores num_runs identical EMPTY recommendation lists against each other, so the variance it reports is 0 by construction whatever the platform is doing. /evaluation/calibration scores the confidences in the request body, and CalibrationProbe states it uses their variance as a proxy because there is no ground truth -- calibration needs realized outcomes, and nothing records one. /evaluation/decision-quality combines four numbers taken as query parameters, defaulting to 0.75/0.05/0.80/0.70, so its 'index' is whatever the caller passes. The module docstring claimed 'No static or mock values' until 2026-09-24; it now names these three as excluded.

evidence.says: - Variance of confidence scores as a proxy for calibration

leaves_by.asserts: each endpoint's answer changes when the platform's recorded behaviour changes, and does not change when only its own request parameters do -- or the endpoints are withdrawn and this entry is retracted

declared_not_implemented.capability: EvidenceGroundingAgent and DomainExpertElicitationAgent produce the outputs AGENTS.md specifies

claimed_in.says: - Evidence citations with relevance scores
- Disagreement flags when expert statements conflict with existing graph assets

declared_not_implemented.reality: Both agents run, and every skill under them is a labelled stub that returns a constant. EvidenceGroundingAgent: evidence retrieval returns no citations, statistical validation returns valid for any non-empty citation, contradiction detection returns none, and the semantic-layer read returns an empty context. DomainExpertElicitationAgent: elicitation returns no assumptions, prior encoding returns the uniform Beta(1,1) whatever the expert said, and disagreement surfacing returns none. The code is honest about this -- each docstring says 'Stub:' and names what production would do -- but AGENTS.md is loaded as shared context by every agent and presents the outputs as capabilities, so the two disagree. No evidence store is populated for the first agent to read, and no elicitation UI exists to feed the second.

evidence.says: Stub: returns empty (no evidence store populated yet).

leaves_by.asserts: each named skill returns a different answer for two inputs that should differ -- citations for a claim with stored evidence and none for one without, a non-uniform prior for a confident expert statement, a disagreement when expert and data conflict -- or the AGENTS.md sections are rewritten to describe what the agents do

declared_not_implemented.capability: The decision thresholds are calibrated rather than merely consistent

claimed_in.says: > target outcome — and is that evidence strong enough to act on without asking a human?

declared_not_implemented.reality: The machinery is built and pinned: every decision seals a follow-up plan carrying the prediction it used, POST /api/v1/decisions/{entry_digest}/followup re-runs that plan's own analysis over a later window, and GET /api/v1/decisions/calibration aggregates. Since septa-10 the report is also built to be trusted when evidence arrives, and proven so on SIMULATED decision streams by the pre-registered C0 gate: a rate only from 10 or more follow-ups, each with a Clopper-Pearson interval (coverage of the constructed truth 0.9575-1.0 over 400 streams per design), undecidable follow-ups counted apart and carried into worst-case bounds over every acted decision, and 'could not resolve' (fewer than 6 discordant pairs) reported apart from 'no difference'. What does not exist is the evidence: no follow-up has been taken on any real operation, so on the platform every rate is refused for want of follow-ups, and C0's figures are about simulated streams, not about these thresholds. This entry leaves the list when a body of real follow-ups exists and the thresholds have been moved (or kept, on the record) by what it showed -- which is operational history, not code.

evidence.says: What happened after the verdict, and whether the verdict deserved to be trusted.

leaves_by.asserts: at least the pre-registered minimum (C0's min_followups, 10) of decidable follow-ups on REAL operations exists in the store, the report states each rate from them with its interval and 'could not resolve' separately from 'no difference' (the report's arithmetic is C0's), and docs/CURRENT_STAGE.md cites that measured calibration figure with the run that produced it, labelled as real rather than simulated

declared_not_implemented.capability: Agents render their prompts from the versioned templates in prompts/

claimed_in.says: Prompt templates are versioned in `prompts/` alongside their schema contracts. No agent uses ad-hoc prompts at runtime.

declared_not_implemented.reality: Nothing in backend/src, packages or frontend/src reads prompts/*.yaml, and no runtime path calls an LLM at all (llm-routing-no-callers). The templates are specification artefacts; prompts/README.md now says so. Ten of the fourteen also carried a duplicate top-level `skill:` key, which no loader had ever complained about because none had ever run.

leaves_by.asserts: a runtime agent renders its prompt from the matching prompts/*.yaml template and fails when the template is missing or malformed -- or AGENTS.md:609 is retracted

declared_not_implemented.capability: Semantic objects are versioned: no in-place mutation, deprecate and replace

claimed_in.says: 2. All objects are versioned — no in-place mutation; deprecate and replace.
No in-place mutation. Deprecate and replace.
All objects are versioned — no in-place mutation (Rule #2)
Version increments on any field change

declared_not_implemented.reality: Approval and rejection UPDATE the object's own row: promote_to_approved rewrites approval_status, approved_at, approved_by, guardian_verdict_ref and lineage, and reject_draft rewrites approval_status (to DEPRECATED) and lineage, and record_edge_sensitivity (septa-62) rewrites a draft edge's assumption_refs and lineage to add the assumption carrying the kernel's sensitivity result. The version column keeps its 1.0.0 default, because no code path increments it and no new row is written for a new version. The previous state survives only as lineage entries and audit_log rows. The interventions feedback endpoint likewise UPDATEs interventions in place.

leaves_by.asserts: approving or rejecting an object leaves the prior row unchanged and writes a successor with an incremented version -- or the versioning claims are retracted from the registry docstring and the docs

declared_not_implemented.capability: Every approved semantic object carries lineage from source data to approver

claimed_in.says: 3. All approved objects carry lineage.
This satisfies EU AI Act Art. 13 lineage
This satisfies EU AI Act Article 13 transparency requirements

declared_not_implemented.reality: Approval and rejection each append one step (APPROVED or REJECTED: actor, time, verdict id), recording a sensitivity result appends a MODIFIED step naming the new assumption and the verdict, and an edge keeps whatever lineage list its submitter sent. Nothing records the data source, the transformation steps or the policy rules into lineage, and no platform code constructs a LineageRecord. An entity's submitted lineage is not stored (the INSERT omits the column). Fragments had no lineage column at all until 006_graph_fragment_lineage.sql, so approving or rejecting one failed outright. The Guardian verdict, its cited rules, and the evidence and assumption ids are linked by reference, so the chain can be partly rebuilt by joins. Nothing shows that this satisfies EU AI Act Art. 13.

leaves_by.asserts: an object submitted, approved and used in an analysis carries lineage naming its source, each transforming agent/skill and version, the verdict and rules, and the approver -- for edges, entities and fragments alike

declared_not_implemented.capability: Continuous distribution, causal, semantic and concept drift monitoring

claimed_in.says: Production-ready with multi-type drift detection (distribution, causal, semantic, concept)
| **Causal drift** | Graph structure diverges from live data patterns | Flag graph fragment for re-review |
| **Concept drift** | Model performance degradation over time | Re-estimation trigger |

declared_not_implemented.reality: The drift functions compute when called directly with data (KL/JS on histograms, a correlation-below-0.5 check labelled causal drift, Jaccard word overlap on definitions, a chi-squared test on labels). DriftMonitorAgent.process, which the periodic sensor runs, hands each skill only a fragment id, so drift_detect returns kl_divergence 0.0 with note no_data_for_comparison, the structure and semantic comparisons return no drift for want of edges and definitions, and concept_drift is passed as False. The pipeline therefore cannot raise a drift alert. Alerts go to an in-process AlertEmitter; the Kafka topic named in its return value has no producer.

leaves_by.asserts: the periodic sensor, run over a fragment whose stored baseline differs from current data by a known shift, raises a drift alert carrying the measured divergence -- and does not for an unshifted copy

declared_not_implemented.capability: The published TypeScript contract matches the backend models field for field

claimed_in.says: MUST implement these core types with exact field alignment
TypeScript interfaces generated from / aligned to the canonical schema

declared_not_implemented.reality: packages/semantic-types/src/entities.ts is written by hand, not generated, and seven of its interfaces declare fields models.py does not have. Treatment, Confounder and Mediator add description, domain, approvalStatus, createdBy, createdAt and lineage; Outcome adds the same plus units; CausalEdge adds createdAt, and declares createdBy non-null where the backend's is optional (null for edges drafted before migration 011); GraphFragment adds approvedBy, approvedAt and lineage; Intervention adds description, domain, graphFragmentRef and approvalReason. A client typed against the package expects fields the API never sends. scripts/contract_parity.py checks only the shared enumerations, not interface fields.

leaves_by.asserts: for every interface in packages/semantic-types/src/entities.ts, the camelCased field set equals the field set of the same-named model in models.py (or the TypeScript is generated from the models)

declared_not_implemented.capability: Runtime data contracts: freshness, schema and semantic checks before agents consume data (Guardian PR-009)

claimed_in.says: Validates a data contract at runtime before agent data consumption, enforcing freshness SLAs, schema compliance, and semantic alignment.
Data contracts enforce freshness SLAs at runtime, not just schema validation
`src/agents/governance.py` enforces PR-009 (implemented)

declared_not_implemented.reality: contracts.py defines the contract, SLA and violation models and a ContractRegistry that can register, look up and remove contracts. Nothing evaluates a contract, nothing produces a ContractViolation, and only the tests instantiate the registry. PR-009 fires only when a caller sends action_type DATA_ACCESS_WITH_CONTRACT, which no code path does, and it reads the violation list from that caller's own payload. So a caller that reports no violations is never blocked.

leaves_by.asserts: an agent reading a data product whose registered contract's freshness SLA has lapsed is refused by the Guardian with PR-009 cited, the violation computed by the platform rather than supplied by the caller -- and a fresh product is not refused

declared_not_implemented.capability: FLARE planning forward-simulates each candidate action with the approved causal model before committing

claimed_in.says: 1. SimulateAhead   — Forward-simulate action consequences using the approved SCM
SimulateAhead (SCM lookahead)
**SimulateAhead**: Forward-simulates each candidate action using the approved
SCM used for effect estimation when approved fragment available

declared_not_implemented.reality: _simulate_single_action calls effect_estimate with data=None, and the kernel refuses without data, so no action ever gets an estimate. Under an APPROVED fragment each action's confidence is halved (action.confidence * 0.5, never a failure). Without a fragment it keeps its own confidence and fails below 0.3. The lookahead is therefore arithmetic on the recommendations' own confidences. Under an APPROVED fragment an action needs confidence >= 0.8 to clear the node's 0.4 commit threshold, while without one it needs 0.4: an approved causal model makes the planner commit less often, not more. SIMULATED_NOT_EXECUTED outcomes are not surfaced. Since 2026-09-26 a plan with no estimate is flagged plan_unsimulated and goes to the Guardian with each recommendation saying it was not simulated (an uncommitted one with requires_human_review); only an estimated failure escalates, and that is not the CHAOTIC domain. When the kernel refuses, the refusal is returned as not-a-failure and the action proceeds at half its prior confidence: a refusal is silently turned into a smaller number instead of reaching the caller.

evidence.says: data=None,  # no observational data here: the kernel refuses, ate is None

leaves_by.asserts: given an APPROVED fragment and observational data in which one candidate action's effect is known to be harmful, the planner's simulated effect for it comes from causal-core and that action is not committed -- and the committed choice changes when the data does

declared_not_implemented.capability: Privacy controls: PII pseudonymization at ingestion, logical erasure, portable export

claimed_in.says: PII fields are **pseudonymized at ingestion**
| Art. 17 – Right to erasure | Pseudonymization + key deletion (logical erasure) |
| Art. 20 – Data portability | Semantic layer export (JSON-LD format) |

declared_not_implemented.reality: No code pseudonymizes, tokenizes or strips any field, no erasure path exists (a provenance erasure, POST /api/v1/provenance/session/{id}/erasure, writes a tombstone that hides a session's provenance from the API and deletes nothing, so it is not Art. 17 erasure), and no JSON-LD (or other) export of the semantic layer exists. No connector runs in the platform, so today PII can enter only through API request bodies, and nothing inspects them for it. The Art. 30 row (records of processing) is the one backed by something real: audit_log.

leaves_by.asserts: a connector run over records containing configured PII fields stores only pseudonymous tokens; deleting a subject's key makes their records unlinkable; and an export endpoint returns the semantic layer in the documented format

declared_not_implemented.capability: The full Rambachan-Roth sensitivity machinery for difference-in-differences: restrictions on consecutive changes in the trend difference (smoothness, relative magnitudes of period-to-period deviations) and their sharper confidence sets
declared_not_implemented.reality: Split from did-extensions when its covariate and not-yet-treated parts left the list (T5 v4). Parallel-trends sensitivity exists since T5 v3 in a simplified, conservative form: relative magnitudes on event-time levels, union-bound intervals, a breakdown multiple. Rambachan & Roth's restriction on consecutive changes and their confidence sets do not exist.

evidence.says: "relative magnitudes on event-time deviations (after Rambachan & Roth 2023): post-adoption "
- The full Rambachan & Roth machinery: their restriction is on consecutive changes, not levels,

leaves_by.asserts: a pre-registered T5 version gates the coverage of Rambachan-Roth confidence sets under planted violations of a consecutive-change restriction, with a seeded defect that bounds levels instead of changes

declared_not_implemented.capability: Difference-in-differences with anticipation windows, repeated cross-sections (no unit observed twice) and time-varying covariates
declared_not_implemented.reality: Split from did-extensions when its covariate and not-yet-treated parts left the list (T5 v4). causal_core.panel needs a balanced panel of units observed in every period, assumes no anticipation, and accepts time-invariant covariates only: a covariate that varies within a unit is refused (INVALID_INPUT), an unbalanced panel is refused (DESIGN_CHECK_FAILED), and there is no anticipation parameter.

evidence.says: Not offered in this version: time-varying covariates, anticipation windows,
"time-invariant, pre-treatment characteristics only; a covariate that changes after "

leaves_by.asserts: each of anticipation windows, repeated cross-sections and time-varying covariates ships with its own pre-registered T5 version and seeded defect, or is retracted from the docs that list it as planned

declared_not_implemented.capability: Cynefin-domain classification that routing, human escalation and Guardian rules can rely on

claimed_in.says: Agents self-classify the domain complexity of a query before selecting a reasoning strategy.
Cynefin domain classification with confidence
Domain confidence > 0.7
when the Cynefin domain classification is CHAOTIC

declared_not_implemented.reality: IncidentTriageAgent._skill_cynefin_classify is a keyword stub. Run on an external labelled corpus of 456 incident-style queries (the CARF Under Test lab's spine/test_set.jsonl, 5 domains), it labels 454 of 456 COMPLEX when no assumptions are active and 449 COMPLICATED when one is: macro F1 0.07, below always guessing the most common domain (0.11), and 0 of 50 CHAOTIC items recalled -- so the CHAOTIC-to-human escalation the docs describe depends on keywords that almost never fire; a TF-IDF naive Bayes baseline reaches 0.92 on the same corpus. It never outputs CLEAR or DISORDER, so the DisorderProtocol branch is unreachable from it. Its confidences are constants (0.60-0.85), so 'domain confidence > 0.7' measures which branch fired, not how likely the label is. Since 2026-09-25 a description no keyword matches is classified DISORDER with confidence 0 (it was COMPLEX, or COMPLICATED when an assumption was active), so the stub's commonest answer now routes to a person instead of to analysis; the two-word keywords could never match until the same day.

evidence.says: A HEURISTIC STUB, and measured as one

leaves_by.asserts: a pre-registered routing gate on a hand-labelled incident-phrasing set reports macro F1 against a most-common-class and a TF-IDF naive-Bayes baseline, per-domain recall with a CHAOTIC floor, calibration with per-bin counts, and the share of inputs it commits to -- and escalation of high-severity or irreversible incidents does not depend on the label at all

declared_not_implemented.capability: Dynamic application security testing (DAST): a scanner such as OWASP ZAP run against a running API, weekly

claimed_in.says: DAST: OWASP ZAP against a staging API (weekly). Not built: there is no staging

declared_not_implemented.reality: Not built. Nothing starts the API and scans it dynamically; there is no staging environment to scan. The container images are built and scanned for known vulnerabilities in CI (job images), which is not DAST.

leaves_by.asserts: a workflow starts the backend (the built image, or a staging deployment) and runs a DAST scanner against its API, failing on findings not in a reviewed allowlist

declared_not_implemented.capability: One-click Rosenbaum / E-value sensitivity analysis on an approved edge, in the UI

claimed_in.says: I want to run a one-click Rosenbaum sensitivity analysis on any approved edge

declared_not_implemented.reality: No UI runs a sensitivity analysis. The kernel reports E-values, robustness values and (for back-door designs with a binary treatment) a Rosenbaum bound on every analysis from data, but nothing in the frontend requests one for an edge; the governance page's sensitivity panel is a hard-coded example whose label conflates the two methods ("Rosenbaum E-value").

leaves_by.asserts: on an approved edge with data, one action shows the kernel's E-value and Rosenbaum gamma* (or its reason for none) from a live analysis, not a fixture

left_the_list.was: The registry checks only that the verdict id exists in audit_log with verdict APPROVED: not that it was issued for this object or payload, not that it is unused, and it carries no signature -- one APPROVED row authorises any number of unrelated writes (replay), and anything that can insert into audit_log can mint one (forge).

/check builds its EpistemicState with no Cynefin domain, which defaults to DISORDER, and Guardian rule PR-006 rejects every verdict in DISORDER -- so /check never returns APPROVED and /approve can never be satisfied through the API.
approve_object never passes the notes on, so they are discarded; a rejection's reason reaches audit_log only inside the SHA-256 payload_hash. No reason text is stored anywhere.
RejectRequest requires verdict_id, but reject_object never reads it: any UUID is accepted.

POST /api/v1/interventions/{id}/approve depends on get_current_user only, with no require_role, so any authenticated user can approve an intervention -- and doing so hand-writes an APPROVED row into audit_log. That row can no longer authorise a semantic-layer write (it is unsigned; see guardian-verdict-binding in left_the_list), but the intervention itself is approved by someone who may hold no governance role.

GovernanceAgent._execute_skill exposes an `audit_write` skill whose verdict comes from its own inputs, defaulting to APPROVED: an agent calling it writes whatever verdict it likes into audit_log. The row cannot authorise a semantic write (it is signed for no subject), but it still enters the audit trail as though the Guardian had ruled.

causal_decision.ledger builds and verifies the chain in memory, with tests for an edited, removed and reordered entry. Nothing in the platform writes a record, serves one, or anchors a head digest anywhere the writer does not control -- so today the chain proves internal consistency of a list somebody is already holding.

causal_decision.decide reads the pooled estimate and ignores result.segments and result.heterogeneity entirely. So an action whose effect is +6 in one segment and -12 in another can be approved on a pooled effect of about -3, which describes nobody. The kernel now detects that case; the decision layer does not yet read it.
left_the_list.note: Reachable over HTTP only from fbb1d71: POST /api/v1/decisions re-declared the query without segment_by until then (backend/tests/integration/test_decisions_query.py).

left_the_list.was: Nothing captures what happened after a verdict. packages/causal-decision holds the procedure to the policy it was given and proves it consistent (D0: 15 scenarios, 8 properties, 6 seeded defects); it cannot say the thresholds are right, and no regret or calibration number exists anywhere in this repository.
left_the_list.note: The loop exists and produces numbers: a plan is sealed with each decision, /followup re-runs that plan's own analysis over a later window, and /calibration aggregates. What it does NOT yet establish is that the thresholds are right -- that needs enough follow-ups to have been taken, which is operational history rather than code. The report reads null for every rate with nothing behind it, so an empty platform cannot read as a calibrated one.

left_the_list.was: session_state and incidents are created only by the SQLite DDL in backend/src/db/factory.py. The PostgreSQL migrations (001-004) never create them, and CloudSqlFactory.init_db runs the DDL only when ENV=local, so on a PostgreSQL deployment session persistence and the incidents API would fail with a missing table. api/incidents.py also writes with INSERT OR REPLACE, which PostgreSQL does not accept. Neither schema has the evidence, preference or simulation-result tables DATA_LAYER.md used to list. The suite runs only against SQLite, so nothing notices.
left_the_list.note: Implemented. Migrations 008_session_state.sql and 009_incidents.sql create the two tables, mirroring SQLITE_DDL column for column (TIMESTAMPTZ times, JSONB payloads, the REVOKE/GRANT convention; neither is append-only, both are upserted). api/incidents.py upserts with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE, which both dialects accept, keeping the first created_at. The leaves_by test runs on PostgreSQL in the new gate step backend-pytest-postgres (tests/conftest.py builds the database from backend/src/db/migrations/*.sql when TEST_DATABASE_URL is set; CI provides a postgres:16-alpine service) and asserts the migrated schema's (table, column) pairs equal SQLITE_DDL's, and that a session snapshot and an incident round-trip. Not changed: the evidence, preference and simulation-result tables DATA_LAYER.md used to list exist in neither schema, and SQLITE_DDL still carries only three of the migrations' CHECK constraints and none of their RLS policies or grants; the parity test compares tables and columns, not types or constraints.

left_the_list.was: The migrations declare RLS policies on causal_entities and causal_edges that read app.user_domains and app.user_role, but no application code sets either, and RLS does not bind the table owner that docker-compose connects as, so the policies isolate nothing; connecting as causal_app would instead hide every row. Roles and domain scope are enforced in the API and the registry's queries (src/middleware/rbac.py), not by the database. graph_fragments has no policy at all.
left_the_list.note: Implemented, on PostgreSQL. Migration 010_rls_binds.sql replaces 001's two policies and gives graph_fragments one, each USING and WITH CHECK app_scope_allows(domain): the domain is in app.user_domains (now a JSON array; 001 split on commas) or no list is set and app.user_role (a JSON array of platform roles) holds governance_officer, platform_engineer or the causal_service marker -- so a present domains claim binds every role, as rbac.domain_scope says, where 001 let those two roles through regardless. src/db/scope.py keeps the scope in a context variable and opens every PostgreSQL transaction with set_config(..., true) for both settings (transaction-local, so pooled connections carry nothing over); the auth middleware binds rbac.scope_for_user(user) per request. Outside a request the scope is empty (nothing visible); code with no user declares service_scope(reason), which is unscoped on purpose (the seeder and the test fixtures' direct calls do). The app connects as causal_app, a non-owner role, rather than FORCE RLS on an owner connection, and refuses to start as a superuser, a BYPASSRLS role or the owner; docker-compose gives causal_app a local-dev login. 010 also grants causal_app USAGE on decision_followups_id_seq, created after 001's blanket grant, without which every followup insert as causal_app failed. The PostgreSQL test fixtures connect the app as causal_app (a per-run member login), so the whole suite runs under RLS. The leaves_by test asserts, over raw SQL as causal_app with the settings set as the app sets them, that a user limited to one domain selects no row of another from the three tables, and includes negative controls (policy dropped, RLS disabled, owner connection) that leak. Not changed: SQLite, the local engine, has no RLS, so there the application's filter is the only line; role checks (which route a role may call) stay in the API; tables without a domain are not scoped.

left_the_list.was: Difference-in-differences beyond the current design: covariate-conditional parallel trends, not-yet-treated comparisons, anticipation, repeated cross-sections, and the full Rambachan-Roth sensitivity machinery. causal_core.panel estimated unconditional group-time effects against never-treated units only.
left_the_list.note: Implemented in part, and the rest split rather than claimed. Covariate-conditional parallel trends (CausalQuery.covariates: each group-time effect is Sant'Anna & Zhao's doubly robust DiD, logistic propensity and linear outcome regression, with an influence function carrying both models' estimation effects) and not-yet-treated comparisons (CausalQuery.control_group) shipped in contract 0.10.0, pre-registered as T5 v4 (fbdbc1a) before the code, and passed its first registered run (benchmarks/t5-did/results/2026-09-26-v4-run1.json, 7b4ce0f): five new designs, including covariate-driven adoption timing where the unconditional estimate is biased by 0.54 and each nuisance model misspecified in turn; three new refusals (poor overlap -> POSITIVITY, time-varying covariate -> INVALID_INPUT, no comparison units -> DESIGN_CHECK_FAILED); four new seeded defects, each caught by its registered bias bar. Limits: under a misspecified outcome model the intervals sit near the coverage band's floor (0.932 in the registered run, 0.914-0.942 on development seeds); linear-index nuisance models only. The Rambachan-Roth machinery is now did-rambachan-roth; anticipation, repeated cross-sections and time-varying covariates are did-anticipation-cross-sections.

left_the_list.was: E-values are now correct and scale-aware (causal-core's e_value_rr; risk ratio, or difference plus outcome SD; otherwise null with the reason), and the kernel reports E-values and Cinelli-Hazlett robustness values from data. Rosenbaum bounds are not implemented: rosenbaum_gamma is always null (the previous values came from an invented multiplier).
left_the_list.note: Implemented, and the UI half split off rather than claimed. Rosenbaum bounds: for a back-door design with a binary treatment, causal_core.analyze builds a 1:1 matched design (greedy nearest neighbour on the propensity-score logit, without replacement, caliper AnalysisPolicy.match_caliper = 0.2 SD) and reports Sensitivity.rosenbaum (contract 0.12.0): Wilcoxon's signed-rank test under Rosenbaum's upper bound (normal approximation, Rosenbaum 2002 4.3.3), the upper-bound p-value by gamma, the matched sample's largest standardized difference, and gamma_star, the largest gamma at which the test -- one-sided in the primary estimate's direction at (1 - ci_level)/2, the level of the primary interval and e_value_ci -- still rejects no effect; randomized designs, non-back-door strategies, continuous treatments and too few pairs get no gamma and a reason (rosenbaum_null_reason). The backend sensitivity_analysis skill takes matched pair_differences and returns rosenbaum_gamma from the kernel. Pinned by test_rosenbaum_bounds.py, which reproduces Rosenbaum's Table 4.3 upper bounds on the Morton et al. (1982) lead pairs (0.0018, 0.0136, 0.0388, 0.0468, 0.0740 at gamma = 2, 3, 4, 4.25, 5), and pre-registered as T9 (730d15c) before the code, first registered run passed (benchmarks/t9-rosenbaum/results/2026-09-26-v1-run1.json, 4f34987): in paired designs drawn from Rosenbaum's model at its worst case, gamma_star reached the planted bias in 2.85% (gamma_0 = 2) and 1.95% (gamma_0 = 4) of runs (bar 3.5%) and retained the conclusion at gamma_0/1.5 in 96.7% and 91.8%; end-to-end with an unmeasured confounder of odds ratio 3, no run claimed gamma_star >= 3 and the median 1.63 tracked the oracle design sensitivity 1.880; three seeded defects caught. Limits: Wilcoxon's statistic only (it understates design sensitivity); greedy 1:1 matching, no full or optimal matching; residual imbalance after inexact matching is bias the bound does not cover; gamma_star speaks to the matched comparison's test of no effect, not to the AIPW/IPW estimate (no marginal sensitivity model for the weighted estimators). The one-click UI of docs/UIX.md US-21 is sensitivity-one-click-ui.

left_the_list.was: PR-007 is in the Guardian's rule table and nowhere in its evaluation: no check reads a sensitivity result, so an edge is approved whether or not any sensitivity analysis was run, and PR-007 is never cited on a verdict. The rules that are evaluated are PR-001 to PR-006, PR-008, and PR-009 (on one action type).
left_the_list.note: Implemented for approvals. A /check for GOVERNANCE_APPROVE whose subject is a stored edge reads the edge's sensitivity results from the database (src/agents/governance.py edge_sensitivity) and is REJECTED citing PR-007 when there are none; evaluated after PR-001, before PR-004, and an unreadable edge fails closed. What counts as an edge's sensitivity result: CausalEdge has no field of its own, so it is a valid SensitivityResult (E-value / Rosenbaum) stored on an assumption the edge names in assumption_refs, that assumption not REJECTED in review; the checked payload cannot supply one. The write path it needs was broken too: propose_draft dropped an assumption's sensitivity_result, and the reads did not decode it; both fixed. Pinned with results from causal_core.analyze on simulated data. Limits: PR-007 asks for a result, not a robust one -- a result that says not robust still counts, and the reviewer sees it (the CYBERSECURITY.md claim, since withdrawn, said 'pass'); proposing an edge (the process() path's proposed_edges) is not approving it and is not judged; until septa-62 nothing in the platform recorded the kernel's sensitivity output on an assumption -- a result arrived only with the assumption's draft; since then POST /api/semantic/edges/{edge_id}/sensitivity and SimulationAgent record it, through a Guardian verdict for RECORD_SENSITIVITY, as a new IGNORABILITY assumption on the draft edge (backend/tests/guardian/test_edge_sensitivity_recorded.py). Since 062f57d a result counts only when the platform recorded it: a drafter could attach one to an assumption they draft (computed_by is free text) and satisfy PR-007 with a made-up number, so record_edge_sensitivity now stores the id of the RECORD_SENSITIVITY verdict it spent (assumptions.sensitivity_verdict_id, migration 013, unique) and src/semantic_layer/review_risk.py recorded_sensitivity counts a result for an edge only when that row is APPROVED, for RECORD_SENSITIVITY, signed, names the edge and was spent by the recording; propose_draft never writes the column. The review queue's tiers read the same results.

left_the_list.was: ReviewQueueItem carries no risk tier and no submitter, the queue is not ordered by risk, and the UI fills riskTier "MEDIUM" and submittedBy "system" for every item.
left_the_list.note: Implemented. GET /api/governance/review-queue returns risk_tier, risk_reasons and submitted_by for each item and orders by tier (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW), oldest first within a tier. The tier is derived from stored fields only, by rules defined in backend/src/semantic_layer/review_risk.py: an edge is CRITICAL below stated confidence 0.5, HIGH below 0.8 or when no stored sensitivity result on an assumption it rests on says it is robust (the results Guardian PR-007 reads: since 062f57d only those the platform recorded under a RECORD_SENSITIVITY verdict for the edge), else MEDIUM; a fragment is HIGH while it names an edge that is not APPROVED, else MEDIUM; an entity is LOW. These are this repository's own rules, not a standard: stated confidence is the proposer's number, so it can only raise a tier, never lower one on its own. submitted_by is the id in created_by; edges had no created_by, so CausalEdge gained one (migration 012_edge_created_by.sql, the SQLite DDL, propose_draft, get_edge), and edges drafted before it show null, which the UI renders as 'not recorded'. The frontend maps the three fields (frontend/src/app/governance/page.tsx) and ReviewQueue shows the reasons as the tier badge's title; pinned on that side by frontend/src/components/governance/__tests__/ReviewQueue.test.tsx and the queue test in frontend/src/app/governance/__tests__/page.test.tsx.

left_the_list.was: Provenance records live in an in-process dict, lost on restart, and DELETE /api/v1/provenance/session/{id} erases a session's records. Since the role matrix that delete needs a governance role (governance_officer or platform_engineer), but it still erases, so the store is not append-only.
left_the_list.note: Implemented. Migration 011_provenance.sql (and its SQLITE_DDL rendering) stores provenance in provenance_entries (PROV records and LLM invocations, the model as JSON, ordered by sequence) and provenance_erasures; src/semantic_layer/provenance_store.py appends and reads, with no update or delete method. causal_app holds SELECT and INSERT only on both tables, and UPDATE and DELETE are trapped by trigger on PostgreSQL and SQLite, so the owner is refused too. DELETE /api/v1/provenance/session/{id} is gone; POST /api/v1/provenance/session/{id}/erasure (governance roles, a reason of at least ten characters) writes a tombstone -- who, when, why, how many entries -- that hides the session's entries up to that point from trace, export and invocations, which return the tombstone instead. Entries written afterwards are served. The pinning test asserts persistence across a new store, the refusals (and on PostgreSQL causal_app's missing privileges), that no provenance route deletes, the tombstone's hiding and keeping, the reason requirement and the role checks. Not changed: the hidden rows remain in the database, readable by its owner and by causal_governance (causal_readonly is not granted SELECT on the entries), so an erasure is not GDPR Art. 17 erasure -- that is still gdpr-controls. The other half of the withdrawn ADR sentence, contract records, is not append-only either: ContractRegistry is an in-memory store with a remove method, which ADR-002 now says, and no flow uses it (data-contracts-not-enforced).

left_the_list.was: store_provenance_record has no call site: nothing outside the tests writes a provenance record, so the provenance API serves only what tests put there.
left_the_list.note: Implemented for the flows that run. POST /api/v1/session/run and /incident append the run's agent, activity, one activity per reasoning step it added, and its input and output entities (digests of the description, the states and each step's inputs and outputs, not their content); GovernanceAgent.check appends a Guardian activity citing its audit_log row in the same transaction as that row, which covers POST /api/governance/check, approvals, rejections, the triage agent's check and the graph's GuardianCheck node; POST /api/v1/decisions appends the data and graph entities (digests, or the registered model's name, version and digest), the analysis activity and the ledger-entry entity under session decision:<entry_digest> (src/semantic_layer/provenance_capture.py). The pinning test drives each route and reads the records back through GET /api/v1/provenance/trace. Still unwired, and not claimed: LLM invocations -- the llm_factory capture hook now writes to the durable store (tested with a stub model), but no runtime path calls get_llm (llm-routing-no-callers); agents do not write provenance themselves, their reasoning steps are recorded by the session route; and a /session/run whose planner finds no safe action escalates before the GuardianCheck node, so its output cites no audit row.

left_the_list.was: causal_core.cluster reports a carryover check (early-minus-late effect in switched blocks, Welch test) as a design check that never changes the status. T8 v1 measured it: with a 30-minute carryover and a 20-minute washout the estimate was biased by -0.086 and covered 0.887, and the check flagged it in 2% of runs. It is not a safeguard; the washout must be chosen from knowledge of the system.
left_the_list.note: Implemented as pre-registered in T8 v2 (46a1eae) before the code, and passed its registered runs (benchmarks/t8-switchback/results/2026-09-26-v2-run1.json, ecfa386, whose git field is 'unknown' because the gate was started outside the checkout; run2, c95af52, repeats it from the checkout, byte-identical otherwise). The check is now the least-squares slope of the outcome over the retained window of each switched block, into- minus out-of-treatment mean slope, Welch on t(K_s - 2), at a new policy level carryover_alpha = 0.05 (contract 0.11.0); a failure makes the result contested, estimate and interval unchanged. Registered run: power 0.918 in material_carryover (tau = 1.5, lambda = 30, washout 20; bias -0.424, coverage 0.122 unchecked), bar 0.8; false alarms 0.054-0.061 in the four designs the washout covers, bar 0.10; every flagged replication contested and no other. Seeded defects carryover_check_blind, check_includes_washout and flag_not_gating each caught by their bar. Limit, recorded rather than claimed away: against v1's long_carryover (tau = 0.3, bias -0.085, a fraction of a standard error) the check fires in 9.5% of runs, and no check on the minutes after the washout can do much better at T8's sizes -- an oracle GLS matched filter knowing lambda and rho has power near 0.13 on paper. The washout must still be chosen from knowledge of the system.
